artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: fidelity detector, index.json stamping, and retrieval-script loud flagging, all phases completed and verified.

completion_data.completion_summary: Built a re-runnable provenance/fidelity detector (literature-fidelity-audit.sh) that stamps a five-value provenance_fidelity field onto 153 ~/Projects/Literature/index.json entries with zero false positives against the 5 disclosed-partial benchmarks, and made literature-search.sh and literature-briefing.sh loudly flag and quarantine non-verified entries with fail-open semantics throughout.

memory_candidates.content: The ~/Projects/Literature corpus has TWO independent doc_id namespaces that must not be conflated: chunks_data.doc_id (SQLite, used by literature-search.sh) is always the bare source directory name (e.g. 'blackburn_2002'); specs/literature-index.json's doc_id (used by literature-briefing.sh per-repo mode) is index.json's own top-level `.id` field, which frequently differs from the directory name (e.g. 'blackburn_2002_book'). A doc_id-keyed lookup written for one script's namespace will silently fail-open for most of the corpus if reused against the other script without adjustment. Discovered via live testing against .literature.db during task 835, not by static inspection.

In ~/Projects/Literature/index.json, some directories' child entries reference a parent_doc value with NO corresponding top-level id row at all (a 'phantom parent' -- e.g. doets_1987, venema_1991, thomason_1984). Any tool that maps a source directory to its index.json entries should resolve by `.path` prefix match against 'sources/<dir>/' rather than by id/parent_doc name matching, and should fall back to writing/reading directly on child entries when no true root entry exists for that directory. A strict 'parent-only' design will silently miss ~15 directories.

When computing a document-level word-ratio (or any per-document aggregate metric) over a corpus where documents may span multiple .md/.pdf files in one directory, aggregate at the whole-document level by summing across ALL files in the directory -- never sample or measure a single file. Single-file sampling in the ~/Projects/Literature corpus flipped ~7 genuinely healthy, fully-converted documents (e.g. blackburn_2002: 0.03 sampled vs 1.044 true aggregate ratio) into false low-ratio flags.
